questions.question: Surah Al-Fajr opens with the divine oath 'By the dawn.' What does the Arabic root of 'al-fajr' literally convey?
options: The slow setting of the sun on the horizon
The bursting open or splitting of light across the darkness
The complete silence of the desert at midnight
The gradual cooling of the air before sunrise
questions.explanation: Layer 1 explains that the root of 'fajr' conveys the sense of something bursting open, describing the precise moment when the first thread of light splits the darkness of night. The dawn itself becomes a sign of Allah's power over creation.

questions.question: True or false: According to Imam al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir, the strongest interpretation of 'ten nights' in verse 2 is that they refer to the first ten nights of Dhul Hijjah, supported by a hadith of Ibn Abbas in Sahih Bukhari.
questions.explanation: Tabari, after weighing chains of narration, gave decisive preference to the first ten nights of Dhul Hijjah, citing the hadith of Ibn Abbas in Sahih Bukhari. Ibn Kathir concurs unequivocally in Tafsir al-Quran al-Azim.

questions.question: What is one of the most widely cited interpretations of 'al-shaf' wa al-watr' (the even and the odd) in verse 3?
options: The even is the moon and the odd is the sun
The even is the day of Arafah and the odd is the day of Eid
The even is the day of Eid al-Adha and the odd is the day of Arafah
The even refers to angels and the odd refers to jinn
questions.explanation: The most widely cited and hadith-supported interpretation, grounded in a narration from Ibn Abbas and confirmed by Imam Qurtubi, holds that al-watr refers to the 9th of Dhul Hijjah (Arafah) and al-shaf' refers to the 10th (Eid al-Adha).

questions.question: True or false: The Arabic word 'hijr' in verse 5 ('an oath sufficient for one of hijr') is rooted in the meaning of restraint, and from this root comes the concept of intellect because it restrains a person from irrational conduct.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir explains that 'hijr' literally means 'to prevent' or 'to restrain,' and 'dhi hijr' means a person of sound mind whose intellect prevents them from acting irrationally. The verse links intellectual integrity to spiritual perception.

questions.question: How does the tafsir describe the people of 'Iram, possessors of lofty pillars' (verse 7) in connection with the people of Aad?
options: They were a tribe of nomads with no permanent settlements
They were known for their towering architecture and were destroyed by a devastating wind
They were a peaceful merchant people who voluntarily accepted Hud's message
They were a coastal seafaring civilization unrelated to Aad
questions.explanation: Tabari and Ibn Kathir describe Aad as a powerful Arabian civilization known for towering architecture (Iram of the lofty pillars) and material prosperity, eventually destroyed by a devastating wind for rejecting Prophet Hud and persisting in arrogance.

questions.question: What distinguishing achievement of the people of Thamud is mentioned in verse 9 ('who carved the rocks in the valley')?
options: They built the first ocean-going ships
They cut their homes directly out of rocky mountains in the valley
They invented a written alphabet still in use today
They constructed the first planned irrigation networks
questions.explanation: Layer 1 explains that Thamud literally cut their homes out of the rocky mountains of the valley. The ruins at Madain Salih, with their rock-cut tombs carved into sandstone, remain as a tangible legacy. Yet their mastery of stone could not save them when they defied Prophet Salih.

questions.question: True or false: Fakhr al-Din al-Razi, in line with Ashari theology, classifies 'bi-al-mirsad' in verse 14 as a metaphor for Allah's complete knowledge and inevitable recompense, rejecting any implication of spatial location for Allah.
questions.explanation: Al-Razi in Mafatih al-Ghayb firmly classifies 'bi-al-mirsad' as a metaphor (isti'arah) for Allah's encompassing knowledge and inevitable recompense, not an attribution of spatial location, consistent with the Ashari and Maturidi consensus that Allah is beyond place and direction.

questions.question: Verse 15 critiques a fundamental human error. What mistaken conclusion does the human make when Allah grants him honor and comfort?
options: That his good fortune was earned by his ancestors
That his Lord has honored him, treating a divine test as a personal reward
That he should immediately give all his wealth to the poor
That his bounty is a curse in disguise
questions.explanation: The verb 'ibtala' means to test, not simply to gift. The human wrongly says 'My Lord has honored me,' confusing a test with a reward. Ibn Kathir notes this is a profound misunderstanding - Allah provides to believer and unbeliever alike, and provision is not a measure of moral standing.

questions.question: True or false: Imam al-Tabari and al-Qurtubi explain that verse 19's condemnation of 'devouring inheritance' refers to the pre-Islamic Arabian practice of giving inheritance only to adult male warriors and excluding women, children, and the disabled.
questions.explanation: Qurtubi, drawing on Tabari's transmissions, details how the Arabs of the Jahiliyya gave inheritance rights only to adult male warriors, entirely excluding women, children, and the disabled. Ibn Kathir adds that the verse also covers the active consumption of orphans' wealth by guardians.

questions.question: According to Sayyid Qutb and Wahbah al-Zuhayli, what is the deeper purpose of verse 20's diagnosis 'and you love wealth with immense love'?
options: To prohibit Muslims from earning any wealth at all
To identify the spiritual root cause of neglecting orphans, the poor, and rightful heirs
To praise those who accumulate wealth through trade
To teach that poverty is itself a sign of divine favor
questions.explanation: Sayyid Qutb sees this verse as capturing the foundational crisis of a society that has made wealth its god. Wahbah al-Zuhayli frames it as establishing 'itidal' (moderation): Islam does not prohibit possession, but excessive love of wealth is the underlying cause of the social crimes condemned in verses 17-19.

questions.question: Ibn Kathir cites a narration from Ibn Abbas that verse 27 ('O reassured soul') was connected to which Companion when revealed?
options: Umar ibn al-Khattab
Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
Uthman ibn Affan
Bilal ibn Rabah
questions.explanation: Ibn Abbas, as reported by Ibn Kathir, narrated that this verse was revealed while Abu Bakr al-Siddiq was sitting with the Prophet, who said, 'This will be said to you.' His soul, nourished by unshakeable certainty, embodied the nafs al-mutmainnah.

questions.question: True or false: In verse 28's pairing 'radiyatan mardiyyah,' the active participle 'radiyatan' describes the soul's own contentment with Allah, while the passive participle 'mardiyyah' describes Allah's pleasure with the soul.
questions.explanation: Ibn Kathir explains that 'radiyatan' is an active participle - the soul is the agent of its own pleasure with its Lord - while 'mardiyyah' is a passive participle indicating the soul receives Allah's approval. Ibn Uthaymeen notes that this rida is the highest spiritual station of the believer.
